prompt: Match each probe to what happens when it fails.
What may a liveness probe check?

choices.text: That the process itself still answers
That the database it uses is reachable and answering queries
choices.why: A restart cannot bring a database back.

choices.text: That every service it calls is ready
choices.why: That restarts it for others' failures.

choices.text: That checkouts succeed end to end

prompt: Why is it reasonable for readiness to check the database, when liveness should not?

choices.text: Readiness runs less often, so the check is cheaper
Readiness is checked only during deploys
Failing it moves traffic away, which helps; a restart would not
Liveness has no access to the network

prompt: With the database stopped, the storefront's `/health` answers ok. What does that tell you about the shop?

choices.text: That checkouts are working
That the database came back by itself after the stop command
That the probe is broken
choices.why: It works; it asks too little.

choices.text: Only that one process is up and responding

prompt: `probe_success` is 1 while nearly every checkout fails. Which signal should page somebody?

choices.text: `probe_success`, after it has been 0 for five minutes
The checkouts' error ratio
The storefront's CPU usage
choices.why: CPU says nothing about failed orders.

choices.text: The number of running containers

prompt: Why does the storefront's readiness not ask `orders`' readiness?

choices.text: Because HTTP calls are not allowed in a probe
Because `orders` has no readiness endpoint
It would take the storefront out for a failure it does not have
Because the storefront has no dependencies

prompt: The orders `/ready` check opens a database and a broker connection on every probe. When does that matter?

choices.text: With many copies probed every few seconds
Never, since connections are free
Only when the database is down
choices.why: It costs when the database is up too.

choices.text: When the database is down, since failed connections take longer
choices.why: It costs when the database is up too.

prompt: What status code does `/ready` return when a dependency fails?

choices.text: 200, with the failure in the body
choices.why: The verdict goes in the code.
Not the one the code returns.

prompt: Docker marks the orders container unhealthy. What does Docker do about it?

choices.text: It restarts the container after three failures in a row, like Kubernetes
Nothing but record it; a restart policy ignores health
It stops sending it traffic
choices.why: Docker routes no traffic by health.

choices.text: It stops the containers that depend on it

prompt: Compose can make one service wait for another with `depends_on` and `condition: service____`, using the status its healthcheck reports.
What does `start_period` in a Docker healthcheck do?

choices.text: Failures during it do not count towards unhealthy
It delays the container's start until the first check has passed
It sets how often the check runs
It sets how long one check may take before it counts as failed

prompt: A pod's readiness probe fails. What happens to it?

choices.text: It is restarted
It is deleted and replaced by a new pod on the same node, with a new name
It is marked not ready and the Service stops sending to it
Nothing happens until the liveness probe fails as well and confirms it

prompt: After a liveness restart, why does the web pod become healthy again?

choices.text: Kubernetes deleted the marker file before restarting, as it does with files in /tmp
The probe was turned off after the restart
The pod moved to another node
A new container starts with a fresh filesystem, without `/tmp/stuck`

prompt: A liveness probe runs every 3 seconds and fails after 3 consecutive failures. About how many seconds pass between the process getting stuck and the kill decision? Answer to the nearest second.
A liveness probe checks the database. The database goes down for ten minutes. What happens?
hint: Every copy checks the same database.

choices.text: One copy restarts and the others keep serving
Every copy restarts, again and again, with growing delays between
The pods move to a node where the database is reachable
Kubernetes pauses the probe until the database returns

prompt: Why does restarting every copy make a database outage worse?
hint: What happens when it comes back.

choices.text: It deletes the data the services were holding in the database
Restarts are billed by the cloud provider
Copies sit in back-off, then all reconnect at once when it returns
The database refuses connections from pods that restarted, until an operator approves them

prompt: Why is a synthetic checkout a better outside check than `/health`?

choices.text: It walks the path a customer takes, through every dependency
It is cheaper to run, since it needs no database of its own to store results
It needs no prober, since Prometheus runs the request itself on each scrape
It never creates data
choices.why: Every probe was a real order.

prompt: Every synthetic checkout is a real order of a kettle. What should a real system do about that? Choose all that apply.
hint: Mark it and keep it out.

choices.text: Mark synthetic requests so they can be told apart
Keep them out of business reports
Use a test card that charges nobody
Run it only once a day so nobody notices

prompt: What can a probe from outside see that no probe inside can?

choices.text: The process's memory
The queue depth, read from outside the broker's own network by the prober
The database's slow queries, which the probe times from the customer's side
DNS, certificates and the network between the customer and you

prompt: A team's pods restart every night at the same time, all together. Liveness checks Redis, which is backed up at that hour. What is the fix?

choices.text: Increase `failureThreshold` until the backup fits
choices.why: The probe would still be wrong.

choices.text: Move the Redis check to readiness and keep liveness local
Remove all probes from the deployment
Move the backup to the afternoon
choices.why: The restarts would move with it.

prompt: Every pod of a service restarts at the same moment. Put the investigation in order.
hint: From the symptom to the probe.
items: See the restart count climbing on every pod
Read the events: the liveness probe failed
Read what the liveness probe checks
Move the dependency check to readiness
